problem: "Fine wire keeps resistance and bulk reasonable" points the wrong way: fine wire has more resistance per metre than thick wire, so it does not keep resistance low. A student may think fine wire lowers resistance, which contradicts the primary/secondary comparison in Section 1.
fix: "Many turns give a higher induced voltage for the same flux change, enough to jump the plug gap. Fine wire lets thousands of turns fit in the core window; its higher resistance is acceptable because the secondary current is very small."

problem: The breaker is said to be "driven by the engine camshaft". In car battery-coil systems the points are opened by a cam on the distributor shaft, which turns at half crankshaft speed; the engine camshaft drives the valves, not the points.
fix: "The contact breaker is a mechanical switch opened by a cam on the distributor shaft, which runs at half crankshaft speed."

problem: "A magneto has a permanent magnet and a coil on the same shaft" is imprecise: in many magnetos the magnet rotates and the coil (armature) is stationary, and the two are not on a common shaft. The next sentence partly corrects this, so the opening line can confuse.
fix: "A magneto has a permanent magnet that rotates past a coil (armature). As the engine turns the magnet, the magnetic flux linking the primary coil changes."
